messages:
carla: heads up — CS escalated: customer 'brightads' in eu-west1 reports p99 generation latency jumped ~4-6x since last night's infra updates. Some requests hit 30s and return 504s. they provided one request id: r-0a9f3c
ben: thanks. did they say this is across models or a single route? any patterns (batch size, seq len)?
carla: they say across text-gen routes, mostly longer contexts (>1k tokens). sample: model=redwood-v2, seq=1600, batch=1. repro from their trace shows long stall during kv-cache fetch step.
dmitri: ok. we shipped CUDA 13.1 + driver 535.42 yesterday to eu-west1 pools and pushed a GPU microcode update to a subset of blades. sounds like host IO spikes + new driver interaction. can you grab node-level logs (dmesg, nvme) and the serving runtime logs?
carla: pasted logs from the customer's node (sanitized):
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 12 timeout, slot 3
[ 1234.568010] nvme nvme0: aborting command
[ 1234.570000] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.572345] nvidia: GPU has stopped responding, Xid 79
```
ben: that nvme timeout + GPU Xid sequence is ugly — suggests NVMe host IO stall coinciding with GPU driver reset. that could explain KV cache stalls and long tail.
dmitri: hypothesis: new driver + microcode exposes a host kernel path where NVMe queue depth or flushes block CPU work needed by our runtime's async IO, causing scheduling stalls for the GPU submission thread. also possible firmware corner-case on certain SSDs.
eva: immediate mitigation options: 1) route affected tenant to fallback pool running pre-update image (driver 530, no microcode) 2) reduce host NVMe qdepth at kernel/qos level 3) enable aggressive kv-cache prefetch/warmup for their traffic 4) throttle long-context requests. which should we do now?
frank: I can flip routing to fallback pool (eu-west1-legacy) right now. that should cut customer p99 while we triage. wants an ETA on rollback?
carla: please do it, customer already hit an incident. do we have a safe rollback for the driver set?
dmitri: rollback plan: revert node image to image-20260104-driver530 which keeps cuda13 but older driver, skip microcode. low-risk. We should also capture bootstrap logs for nodes that hit Xid and run `nvme list`, `nvme monitor`, `iostat -x 1` for 30s during repro.
eva: ops-bot — initiate route change and create ephemeral canary for 5% of the affected pool, then 100% if checks pass. add health checks: p95 < 1s, p99 < 3s for 10m.
ops-bot: Route change started: switching brightads -> eu-west1-legacy (canary 5%). Health checks: p95/p99 monitoring enabled.
ben: also ask CS to run a short synthetic reproducer hitting long contexts: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"...","max_tokens":1500}' and capture timings. add `X-Request-ID` header.
carla: CS confirms canary cut. they're seeing p99 drop to ~900ms for now.
dmitri: great. collect samples from before/after and correlate with node dmesg. if we see NVMe aborts tied to the time window, open bug with SSD vendor + driver team. also check kernel ring buffer for softirqs or CPU stalls. run `perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` on suspect node once we can repro.
frank: starting rollback to image-20260104-driver530 on 3 affected blades (eu-west1-blade-12/13/14). ETA ~18m.
eva: I'll keep the customer update loop open. recommend we also temporarily increase API timeouts for that tenant to 35s so retries don't cascade.
carla: adding followups: 1) rollback complete? 2) gather nvme/nvidia logs from affected blades 3) run controlled repro on the rolled-back nodes 4) if rollback fixes, schedule staged re-roll of driver with additional nvme qdepth tuning and monitoring.
ops-bot: Rollback completed on 3 blades. Post-rollback health: p95 0.6s, p99 1.2s (10m).
dmitri: looks promising. I'll open an internal ticket with infra kernel/driver team: include dmesg snippets, NVMe vendor/model, firmware, driver version, and repro steps. tag: infra/driver/ssd.
carla: customer on hold to confirm for 30m, CS will follow up and verify SLA window. thanks team. :thumbsup:
frank: filing followup runbook: - when p99 spike correlated with Xid & nvme abort -> route tenant to legacy pool, collect logs, rollback image. I'll paste runbook into ops-runbooks channel.
ben: closing loop: assign owner dmitri for root-cause followup with driver and SSD vendor.
cs-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-334 created, severity: high, assigned: dmitri.
carla: marking resolved for customer for now, keep thread open until root cause triaged.
